{"questions": [
{
"id": "p1",
"topic": "functions on a finite set (idempotent maps)",
"error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "Let S = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}. How many functions f : S → S satisfy f(f(x)) = f(x) for every x in S?",
"answer": 1057,
"target_wrong": 1056,
"error_description": "The casework is by the size k of the image of f. The case k = 6 (the image is all of S, forcing f to be the identity) is left out, dropping exactly 1 function.",
"cases": ["image size 1: 6 functions", "image size 2: C(6,2)*2^4 = 240", "image size 3: C(6,3)*3^3 = 540", "image size 4: C(6,4)*4^2 = 240", "image size 5: C(6,5)*5^1 = 30", "image size 6: identity, 1 function"],
"solution": "The condition f(f(x)) = f(x) says every element of the image T = f(S) is a fixed point of f. Conversely, if f fixes every element of some set T and maps every element outside T into T, then f(f(x)) = f(x) for all x. So f is determined by choosing the image T (say |T| = k) and then choosing, for each of the 6 − k elements outside T, one of the k elements of T as its value. The number of such functions is C(6,k)·k^{6−k}. Summing over k = 1,...,6: 6·1 + 15·16 + 20·27 + 15·16 + 6·5 + 1·1 = 6 + 240 + 540 + 240 + 30 + 1 = 1057.",
"check_code": "from itertools import product\nS = range(6)\ncnt = 0\nfor f in product(S, repeat=6):\n    if all(f[f[x]] == f[x] for x in S):\n        cnt += 1\nprint(cnt)"
},
{
"id": "p2",
"topic": "divisor pairs / Egyptian fraction equation",
"error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "Find the sum of the positive integers x for which there exists a positive integer y with 1/x + 1/y = 1/6.",
"answer": 145,
"target_wrong": 133,
"error_description": "The equation becomes (x−6)(y−6) = 36 and the solution lists factor pairs of 36. The pair (6, 6), giving x = y = 12, is left out (the square factorization where the two factors coincide), dropping 12 from the sum.",
"cases": ["(x-6,y-6)=(1,36): x=7", "(2,18): x=8", "(3,12): x=9", "(4,9): x=10", "(6,6): x=12", "(9,4): x=15", "(12,3): x=18", "(18,2): x=24", "(36,1): x=42"],
"solution": "Clearing denominators, 6(x + y) = xy, so xy − 6x − 6y + 36 = 36, i.e. (x − 6)(y − 6) = 36. Since x, y > 0 and 1/x < 1/6 forces x > 6 (similarly y > 6), both factors are positive integers. The ordered factorizations of 36 are (1,36), (2,18), (3,12), (4,9), (6,6), (9,4), (12,3), (18,2), (36,1), giving x − 6 ∈ {1,2,3,4,6,9,12,18,36}, so x ∈ {7,8,9,10,12,15,18,24,42}. The sum is 7+8+9+10+12+15+18+24+42 = 145.",
"check_code": "total = 0\nfor x in range(1, 100000):\n    if x > 6 and (6 * x) % (x - 6) == 0:\n        total += x\nprint(total)"
},
{
"id": "p3",
"topic": "permutations / cycle types",
"error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "Let σ be a permutation of {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}, and let σ^6 denote σ composed with itself six times. How many permutations σ satisfy σ^6(x) = x for every x in {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}?",
"answer": 396,
"target_wrong": 276,
"error_description": "The count is by cycle type with all cycle lengths dividing 6. The mixed cycle type 3+2+1 (one 3-cycle, one 2-cycle, one fixed point), which contributes 120 permutations, is omitted.",
"cases": ["1^6: 1", "2+1+1+1+1: 15", "2+2+1+1: 45", "2+2+2: 15", "3+1+1+1: 40", "3+3: 40", "3+2+1: 120", "6: 120"],
"solution": "σ^6 is the identity exactly when every cycle length of σ divides 6, i.e. every cycle has length 1, 2, 3, or 6. The partitions of 6 into parts from {1,2,3,6} and the number of permutations of each type are: 1^6: 1; 2·1^4: C(6,2)=15; 2^2·1^2: C(6,2)C(4,2)/2 = 45; 2^3: 6!/(2^3·3!) = 15; 3·1^3: C(6,3)·2 = 40; 3^2: 6!/(3^2·2) = 40; 3·2·1: C(6,3)·2·C(3,2) = 120; 6: 5! = 120. Total 1 + 15 + 45 + 15 + 40 + 40 + 120 + 120 = 396.",
"check_code": "from itertools import permutations\ncnt = 0\nfor p in permutations(range(6)):\n    ok = True\n    for x in range(6):\n        y = x\n        for _ in range(6):\n            y = p[y]\n        if y != x:\n            ok = False\n            break\n    if ok:\n        cnt += 1\nprint(cnt)"
},
{
"id": "p4",
"topic": "digit patterns / counting",
"error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "How many four-digit positive integers have the property that the product of their digits equals 36?",
"answer": 72,
"target_wrong": 66,
"error_description": "The count is over multisets of four nonzero digits with product 36. The multiset {2,2,3,3} (two repeated pairs, 6 arrangements) is omitted.",
"cases": ["{1,1,4,9}: 12 arrangements", "{1,1,6,6}: 6", "{1,2,2,9}: 12", "{1,2,3,6}: 24", "{1,3,3,4}: 12", "{2,2,3,3}: 6"],
"solution": "No digit can be 0, so all digits are in {1,...,9}. Write 36 = 2^2·3^2 as a product of four digits (unordered). Possibilities: {1,1,4,9}, {1,1,6,6}, {1,2,2,9}, {1,2,3,6}, {1,3,3,4}, {2,2,3,3}. Count arrangements of each: 4!/2! = 12, 4!/(2!2!) = 6, 12, 24, 12, 6. Since no digit is 0, every arrangement is a valid four-digit number. Total 12 + 6 + 12 + 24 + 12 + 6 = 72.",
"check_code": "cnt = 0\nfor n in range(1000, 10000):\n    p = 1\n    for d in str(n):\n        p *= int(d)\n    if p == 36:\n        cnt += 1\nprint(cnt)"
},
{
"id": "p5",
"topic": "quadratics with integer roots",
"error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "Find the sum of the positive integers k with k ≤ 100 for which the equation x^2 − 20x + k = 0 has an integer solution.",
"answer": 715,
"target_wrong": 615,
"error_description": "Casework on the root pair (r, s) with r + s = 20, r ≤ s. The boundary pair (10, 10), a double root giving k = 100 (exactly at the limit k ≤ 100), is omitted.",
"cases": ["(1,19): k=19", "(2,18): k=36", "(3,17): k=51", "(4,16): k=64", "(5,15): k=75", "(6,14): k=84", "(7,13): k=91", "(8,12): k=96", "(9,11): k=99", "(10,10): k=100"],
"solution": "If r is an integer root, the other root is s = 20 − r, also an integer, and k = rs. Since k > 0 and r + s = 20 > 0, both roots are positive. Taking r ≤ s, the pairs are (1,19), (2,18), ..., (10,10), giving k = 19, 36, 51, 64, 75, 84, 91, 96, 99, 100, all at most 100. Their sum is 19+36+51+64+75+84+91+96+99+100 = 715.",
"check_code": "total = 0\nfor k in range(1, 101):\n    if any(x * x - 20 * x + k == 0 for x in range(-200, 201)):\n        total += k\nprint(total)"
},
{
"id": "p6",
"topic": "dice probability (m+n)",
"error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "Three fair six-sided dice are rolled. The probability that one of the three numbers rolled is equal to the sum of the other two can be written as m/n, where m and n are relatively prime positive integers. Find m + n.",
"answer": 29,
"target_wrong": 43,
"error_description": "Casework on the multiset {a, b, a+b}. The case (1,1,2), where the two summands are equal and smallest (3 ordered outcomes), is omitted, giving 42/216 = 7/36 instead of 45/216 = 5/24.",
"cases": ["{1,1,2}: 3 orderings", "{1,2,3}: 6", "{1,3,4}: 6", "{2,2,4}: 3", "{1,4,5}: 6", "{2,3,5}: 6", "{1,5,6}: 6", "{2,4,6}: 6", "{3,3,6}: 3"],
"solution": "The largest value c must equal the sum of the other two, a + b = c, with a, b ≥ 1 and c ≤ 6. For each c the unordered pairs {a,b} with a + b = c, a ≤ b: c=2: {1,1}; c=3: {1,2}; c=4: {1,3},{2,2}; c=5: {1,4},{2,3}; c=6: {1,5},{2,4},{3,3}. Each multiset with three distinct values has 6 orderings and each with a repeated value has 3: {1,1,2}:3, {1,2,3}:6, {1,3,4}:6, {2,2,4}:3, {1,4,5}:6, {2,3,5}:6, {1,5,6}:6, {2,4,6}:6, {3,3,6}:3, total 45. The probability is 45/216 = 5/24, so m + n = 29.",
"check_code": "from fractions import Fraction\nfrom itertools import product\nfav = 0\nfor a, b, c in product(range(1, 7), repeat=3):\n    if a == b + c or b == a + c or c == a + b:\n        fav += 1\np = Fraction(fav, 216)\nprint(p.numerator + p.denominator)"
},

"id": "p7",
"topic": "functions / fixed points",
"error_type": "misread_condition",
"question": "Let S = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}. How many functions f : S → S have exactly two fixed points, that is, exactly two elements x in S with f(x) = x?",

"topic": "lattice paths / inclusion-exclusion",

"question": "A lattice path from (0,0) to (6,6) consists of unit steps, each either to the right or upward. How many such paths pass through at least one of the points (2,2) and (4,3)?",

"cases": [],

{
"id": "p9",
"topic": "recursively defined sequence / floor of square root",
"error_type": "off_by_one",
"question": "A sequence is defined by a_1 = 1 and a_n = a_{n−1} + ⌊√n⌋ for n ≥ 2, where ⌊t⌋ denotes the greatest integer not exceeding t. Find a_{100}.",
"answer": 625,
"target_wrong": 624,
"error_description": "The solution treats the last block as ⌊√n⌋ = 9 for all 81 ≤ n ≤ 100 (20 terms contributing 180), forgetting that n = 100 is a perfect square with ⌊√100⌋ = 10; the correct block contributes 9·19 + 10 = 181.",
"cases": [],
"solution": "Since a_1 = 1 = ⌊√1⌋, we have a_n = Σ_{k=1}^{n} ⌊√k⌋. For each integer m from 1 to 9, ⌊√k⌋ = m for exactly the 2m+1 integers k from m^2 to (m+1)^2 − 1, all of which are ≤ 99. The lone remaining term is k = 100 with ⌊√100⌋ = 10. Thus a_{100} = Σ_{m=1}^{9} m(2m+1) + 10 = 2·(1^2+...+9^2) + (1+...+9) + 10 = 2·285 + 45 + 10 = 625.",
"check_code": "from math import isqrt\na = 1\nfor n in range(2, 101):\n    a += isqrt(n)\nprint(a)"
},
{
"id": "p10",

"error_type": "misapplied_formula",
"question": "How many functions f : {1, 2, 3, 4} → {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6} satisfy f(1) + f(2) + f(3) + f(4) = 12?",
"answer": 125,
"target_wrong": 165,
"error_description": "Stars and bars is applied to a+b+c+d = 12 with each variable ≥ 1, giving C(11,3) = 165, while ignoring the upper bound of 6 on each value; the 40 solutions with some variable ≥ 7 are not removed.",
"cases": [],
"solution": "We count solutions to a + b + c + d = 12 with 1 ≤ a,b,c,d ≤ 6. Ignoring the upper bound, the number of positive solutions is C(11,3) = 165. Subtract solutions where some variable is ≥ 7: if a ≥ 7, put a = a' + 6 with a' ≥ 1, so a' + b + c + d = 6 has C(5,3) = 10 positive solutions; there are 4 choices of the large variable, giving 40. Two variables ≥ 7 would need sum ≥ 16 > 12, impossible. So the count is 165 − 40 = 125.",
"check_code": "from itertools import product\ncnt = sum(1 for f in product(range(1, 7), repeat=4) if sum(f) == 12)\nprint(cnt)"
}
]}
